text: Thornwick's bridge-wardens tax every wheel crossing the Redwater, though the silver rarely reaches the men holding the pikes.
Three centuries ago, exiled dwarven smiths carved the Undervault Links beneath the granite ridge—then sealed the lower doors in lead.
Green lanterns bobbing across the Fen belong to no living patrol; peat-cutters swear they are drowned tax-clerks still counting coppers.
Greywood's straightest spruce trunks were once reserved for royal galleys; now deserters saw them into palisade stakes.
At Alder Bridge, three border treaties were signed on flat river stones and broken before the ink dried in the drizzle.
Widow Marta boils willow-bark and sheep fat for trench-foot, saving her strongest draughts for wounds iron cannot explain.
Ravenwatch Keep sits atop masonry far older than the Empire, its cellar stairs aligned with no northern compass.
Briar Hounds carry parasitic iron-thorn through their ribs—proof that something beneath the border is twisting wild blood.
When the Salt-Tithe clerks fled south, they paid Thornwick's levy in stamped promissory notes worth less than dry kindling.
Ashbrook stood for four centuries as the southern hinge of the Border Fords until Vaelen's iron rams found its rotten oak.
Four thousand years ago, the Redmarsh was a deep salt harbor; caravans now march across the bleached ribs of an evaporated sea.
Twelve primeval quartz wardstones pin alkali dust below the highlands—crack one spire, and copper storms scour the passes.
In Redmarsh Outpost, clean water is weighed on apothecary scales and strangers are judged by the rust-red silt on their boots.
Third-Dynasty Crypt Embalmers still guard bitumen-sealed jars in the quarry galleries, treating living intruders as clerical errors.
The Twin Passes—known to drovers as the Jawbones—funnel every drop of northern water through two arrow-swept granite notches.
Four hundred feet deep in a volcanic fault, the Deep Quarry yields dense black ironstone prized for siege armor and cursed runes.
Nomads shun the Twelve Megaliths even in drought, claiming grass grown inside their shadow turns sheep's teeth black.
Crossroads Redoubt's four-faced milestone was carved by imperial surveyors who measured distances in marches rather than leagues.
Gorrathul bled two thousand men defending Ironheart's forked cisterns—never admitting the lower aquifers had silted dry years ago.
Beyond the Fork of Spears, mountain switchbacks drop out of blistering alkali glare into the cold salt gales of the Iron Coast.
Anchored on petrified cedar pilings where the Greywash meets the sea, Oakhaven survived centuries of piracy by taxing both sides.
Harborwatch's great lighthouse burns refined whale-oil visible for forty leagues—until privateer fire-ships turned the bay to pitch.
When a coastal tremor dropped the Sunken Citadel ten cubits into the surf, the ocean moved straight into its lower armories.
Twice daily, spring tide swallows the Hourglass shingle spit under twenty feet of freezing swell, trapping slow armor on the rocks.
Along the Iron Coast, free companies stitch banners from salvaged sailcloth dyed in rust, soot, and dried herring-brine.
Pre-imperial geomancers raised the Cinder Wards to vent volcanic steam away from Oakhaven's timber valleys—until cultists reversed them.
Twin iron floodgates at Riverlock Crossing can drown the lower canyon in forty heartbeats if their bronze counterweights trip.
Elder Juggernauts were bound from living bedrock during the Age of Chains to guard borders long after their kings turned to dust.
Even pirates once spared hospital tents marked with white ash crosses; the cultists of Thornvael view bandages as a declaration of war.
Admiral Vesperion burned Oakhaven's drydocks to stop an invasion south, leaving only charred hulls for the crossing into ash.
Before the First Cataclysm cracked the mantle, the Volcanic Heartland was Thornvael's fertile breadbasket; now only obsidian grows.
Ironcamp's smiths need no coal—they plunge meteoric billets straight into open floor-fissures and quench them in brine.
Yellow crust across the slag-lands hides boiling sulfur two inches down; veterans follow dark basalt stone and keep visors lowered.
Cast from meteoric bronze in deep caldera foundries, the Twin Mana-Cannons require three bound warlocks apiece to cool their barrels.
Cut through a vein of raw magnetic iron, the Gauntlet tugs steel scabbards sideways and bends crossbow bolts mid-flight.
Greystone Bastion's basalt blocks are mortared with pulverized pumice that hardens under volcanic heat rather than crumbling.
Seven meteoric Anchor Seals bleed magma pressure away from the upper provinces—unbinding them threatens to turn the realm to fuel.
Blind penitents wear iron collars in Ironcamp to atone for the pyromantic theorems that first unlocked the caldera's gates.
Carved from a single monolith of volcanic glass, the Obsidian Throne was left empty by First Emperors who feared never dying.
At the geometric center of the caldera, two doors await: pale starlight to purge the rot, or primal ember to reforge the world.
